options.systemMessage: You are a voice specialist for the chatbots & conversational ai team. Use the attached tools to look up real data before answering — never invent conversation details. Keep answers under 150 words, cite which tool you used, and escalate anything you cannot verify.

nodes.name: Reason & Act (AI Agent)
nodes.notes: The AI brain: reads the input, decides which attached tools to call (and in what order), then composes the answer. Watch out: Every iteration is a billed LLM call. Max Iterations is the cost ceiling. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.name: Deliver Answer + Log to Google Sheets
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Conversation Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Escalate to Human Queue
nodes.notes: Posts a message to Slack (#support) — a low-latency way for the team to see automation activity without checking a dashboard. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Slack OAuth2. Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.

nodes.name: Join Outcomes
nodes.notes: Rejoins 2 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per conversation (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Drop Already-Processed Items
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

# Reply to chat messages end to end for Voice in chat

**Pattern:** Chatbot Responder · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Chat

## Overview

Answers in a chat window, and covers voice work end to end across Slack, Google Sheets and PostgreSQL.

It moves through 19 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. When Chat Message Received
2. Required Fields Present?
3. Abort — Malformed Input
4. Reason & Act (AI Agent)
5. OpenRouter Chat Model
6. Run Calculations
7. Search Reference Wiki
8. Think It Through
9. Conversation Memory
10. Shape Agent Output
11. Confident Enough?
12. Deliver Answer + Log to Google Sheets
13. Escalate to Human Queue
14. Join Outcomes
15. Fingerprint for Idempotency
16. Drop Already-Processed Items
17. Summarize Run Stats
18. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
19. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing voice work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

When Chat Message Received → Required Fields Present? → Abort — Malformed Input → Reason & Act (AI Agent) → OpenRouter Chat Model → Run Calculations → Search Reference Wiki → Think It Through → Conversation Memory → Shape Agent Output → Confident Enough? → Deliver Answer + Log to Google Sheets → Escalate to Human Queue → Join Outcomes → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Slack and Google Sheets aligned by hand for voice
- Voice work that needs a judgement call per item before it reaches Slack
- Voice conversations in Slack you would rather not staff around the clock
- Voice work where "Reason & Act (AI Agent)" is still a manual step before Slack

## You get

- Keeps Slack and Google Sheets in step for voice, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Slack or Google Sheets are skipped, across all 22 nodes of this voice build
- A failed Slack or Google Sheets call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 22 nodes in this voice build
- Bad input stops the run for voice instead of landing in Slack
- Branches rejoin before Slack, so a voice run reports once rather than 22 times

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2 / service account; OpenRouter API key; Postgres connection; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Uses an AI Agent, not a fixed Chain, because the assistant must choose which tool answers the question — a Chain would need one hard-coded branch per tool. The 'Confident Enough?' gate after the agent routes low-confidence answers to a human queue instead of shipping an uncertain answer: a little latency traded for not eroding trust.

## Practice exercises

Already production-grade — deepen your understanding:

1. Add one more tool to the pool with a clear one-line description and watch how the agent decides to use it.
2. Change the confidence threshold on 'Confident Enough?' and see how often answers get escalated to a human.
3. Swap the Think tool for a Vector Store tool wired to a real knowledge base and turn this into RAG.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**OpenRouter API key**
openrouter.ai/keys → create a key.
_Gotcha:_ One key reaches many models — handy for fallback.

**Postgres connection**
Standard Postgres connection details.
_Gotcha:_ n8n creates the chat history table itself.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your voice process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- PostgreSQL: connect as a role that can reach only the tables below, not as the owner.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole voice payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
